hints: Notice that lactic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$, contains both functional groups needed for ester formation in the same molecule.
Remember an ester forms when a $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ group reacts with an $\text{-OH}$ group, so check which part loses $\text{-OH}$ and which loses $\text{H}$.
Compare the alcohol fragment in 1 and 3, one has lost its $\text{OH}$ to form $\text{-O-CO-}$ and the other still shows $\text{CH(OH)}$, then decide which can exist.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two functional groups**

Lactic acid is a hydroxycarboxylic acid. It has a carboxylic acid group and a secondary alcohol group in the same molecule.

$$ \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H} $$

**Recall self-esterification**

When heated alone, the $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ of one molecule can esterify the $\text{-OH}$ of another molecule, with loss of water.

$$ \text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{HOR'} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} $$

**Check structure 1, the open-chain dimer**

In 1, the second lactic acid unit appears as $\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)CO}_2\text{H}$. Its alcoholic $\text{OH}$ has been replaced by $\text{O-CO-}$. That is exactly correct ester formation, so 1 can form.

**Check structure 2, the cyclic dimer**

If two molecules react twice, head to tail, both $\text{OH}$ groups and both $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups are used to make two ester links. This gives the six-membered cyclic diester called lactide, so 2 can form.

**Check structure 3 and conclude**

In 3, the fragment is written as $\text{-CO}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. The $\text{CH}$ still carries its $\text{OH}$, which is impossible for an ester linkage. The alcohol carbon must lose $\text{OH}$ to become $\text{CH(O-CO-)}$. So 3 cannot form. Only 1 and 2 are possible.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all possible. While 1 and 2 are correct self-esterification products, 3 still shows an $\text{OH}$ group on the esterified alcohol carbon as $\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, which cannot happen in a normal ester.
options.B: This option states 1 and 2 only. Structure 1 is the linear dimer ester $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CO}_2\text{H}$ and structure 2 is the cyclic dimer lactide, both formed by correct reaction of $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ with alcoholic $\text{OH}$ with loss of water.
options.C: This option includes 3 but excludes 1. Structure 3 is invalid because the alcohol part has not lost its $\text{OH}$, whereas structure 1 is a perfectly valid linear ester and should be included.
options.D: This option includes only 1. Structure 1 is correct, but structure 2, the cyclic diester formed by two intermolecular esterifications between two lactic acid molecules, is also very readily formed on heating and should not be excluded.
